analyzed_vuln.description: `xmlRemoveID` passes `attr->id->value` directly to `xmlHashRemoveEntry(...)`. The hash removal callback (`xmlFreeIDTableEntry` -> `xmlFreeID`) frees the same `attr->id` object, so after removal returns, `xmlRemoveID` is still using memory derived from `attr->id` during the call path, causing a heap-use-after-free in this routine. The bug is a lifetime/aliasing issue: key data is taken from an object that is freed as a side effect of hash removal.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered when freeing an attribute marked as ID (`xmlFreeProp` calls `xmlRemoveID`) and that ID is present in `doc->ids`. In this PoV, XML parsing creates duplicate/complex ID state via DTD/entity expansion, then node-copy error cleanup (`xmlStaticCopyNode` -> `xmlFreeNode` -> `xmlFreeProp`) attempts ID removal. `xmlRemoveID` removes the hash entry using `attr->id->value`; removal frees `attr->id`, leading to UAF on that same object in `xmlRemoveID` execution path.
